transcript:
Header: 2026-05-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Nina Zhou (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (AtlasMed Head of Security), Jamal Ortiz (AtlasMed Infra Lead), Priya Narang (AtlasMed Identity Engineer)

[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call real quick, Nina and I are here from Redwood.
[00:06] Laura Kim: Hi, Laura here. Jamal and Priya also on.
[00:09] Jamal Ortiz: Yup, Jamal.
[00:11] Priya Narang: Priya joining.
[00:13] Samir Patel: Great. Today's agenda: go through SSO/SAML setup, SCIM provisioning, RBAC mapping and least-privilege, and touch on audit logs, encryption and data residency — and then outline next steps for the pilot.
[00:25] Nina Zhou: I'll jump into the technical bits after Samir covers the high level.
[00:29] Laura Kim: We're mostly interested in how tight the IAM controls are and whether we can use our IdP (Okta) with SCIM for provisioning and have CMK for encryption.
[00:38] Samir Patel: Totally, that's the plan. Quick note: some of the docs I'll reference are in the security pack I'll share after the call — SOC2 and ISO certs included.
[00:46] Priya Narang: Perfect. We have some specifics: NameID format, group claims, and we prefer just-in-time provisioning only for contractors. Full provisioning via SCIM for employees. Also need audit log retention for 12 months ideally.
[00:59] Samir Patel: Ok noted. We support SAML 2.0, typical setups with IdP metadata upload or metadata URL. Our ACS URL is standard, and we can support NameID formats email and persistent.
[01:12] Jamal Ortiz: Do you enforce signed assertions and want specific digest algorithms? Our security team requires SHA-256 signed assertions.
[01:20] Nina Zhou: Yes, we require signed assertions; SHA-256 is supported. We also recommend enabling encrypt assertions if you need extra protection but most customers keep TLS for in-transit and signed assertions as baseline.
[01:34] Laura Kim: How do you handle SCIM? We want group sync mapped to RBAC roles: engineering -> dev role, security -> admin-read-only?
[01:43] Nina Zhou: We have a SCIM 2.0 endpoint that supports push provisioning from the IdP. For groups we support group-to-role mapping; we can map SCIM group names to Redwood roles in the account admin console. Example: scim group 'atlas-eng' -> role 'developer', 'secops' -> role 'security-admin'.
[02:02] Priya Narang: Any limits on SCIM attributes? We need to sync employeeID, manager, groups, and custom attributes for departments.
[02:11] Nina Zhou: We accept standard attributes (userName, emails, externalId) and a set of custom attributes as an extension. There can be slight name mangling in the auto-generated mapping but we can provide a sample mapping file.
[02:24] Jamal Ortiz: How does deprovisioning work? We need immediate revocation when a user is deactivated in Okta.
[02:31] Nina Zhou: When the user is deactivated via SCIM we can mark them disabled immediately; we also recommend turning on session invalidation which will terminate active tokens/sessions. There's a small propagation window — typically under 2 minutes in hosted mode; for Dedicated/Private we can run closer to realtime but depends on your network.
[02:50] Laura Kim: Audit logs: what do you capture and how long are they retained?
[02:55] Samir Patel: By default hosted accounts have 90 days of audit logs in console; we offer extended retention add-ons (up to 1 year or longer) as a paid addon. Logs include admin actions, role changes, API key usage, token issuance and model request metadata (not PII).
[03:12] Priya Narang: We need at least 12 months immutable audit logs for compliance. Is immutability guaranteed?
[03:18] Nina Zhou: For enterprise accounts on Dedicated or Private, we can integrate with your SIEM or log storage (S3/GCS) and you can set object lock policies for immutability. We can also ship logs to your Kinesis/CloudWatch or secure bucket.
[03:33] Jamal Ortiz: Data residency — we need data at rest in eu-central-1 for our EU customers.
[03:39] Samir Patel: We support region pinning for hosted in certain regions; for strict residency customers we recommend Dedicated in the target region or a Private deployment inside your VPC.
[03:50] Laura Kim: Encryption at rest — can we use our own KMS?
[03:54] Nina Zhou: Yes, we support customer-managed keys. For hosted we can integrate with cloud KMS (customer project/CMK) in AWS KMS or GCP KMS; for Private you can use an HSM. We also support envelope encryption. We'll need to capture who manages rotation and any key policies.
[04:12] Priya Narang: Is there support for BYOK and HSM-backed keys?
[04:16] Nina Zhou: Yes, BYOK and HSM integration are supported for Private deployments and in Dedicated via partner integrations.
[04:24] Laura Kim: For RBAC, can you show typical roles and what least-privilege mapping looks like?
[04:29] Nina Zhou: Default roles: Owner, Admin, Developer, Billing, Read-Only. You can create custom roles scoped to projects and models. Least privilege pattern: give Devs only inference and model-read, Admins manage config but not billing, Owners can manage everything. For sensitive workloads we recommend no direct download access to model weights and restrict model upload permissions.
[04:52] Jamal Ortiz: Do roles support resource-level scoping? e.g., project X only?
[04:56] Nina Zhou: Yes, roles can be scoped per project and per route. We also support attribute-based access rules tied to SCIM groups in the mapping.
[05:06] Samir Patel: Quick aside — in the console we show an audit trail for role changes with who/when and link to the API call.
[05:14] Laura Kim: Are API keys considered high privilege? How do you recommend handling service accounts?
[05:19] Nina Zhou: API keys are high privilege; we recommend fine-grained service account tokens with least-privilege scopes and short TTLs. For long-lived service integrations use token rotation and key-wrapping via KMS. We also support OAuth2 client credentials for some integrations.
[05:36] Priya Narang: How about SAML attribute mapping — do you support groups in the SAML assertion instead of SCIM?
[05:41] Nina Zhou: We can consume group claims in SAML assertions, but SCIM is preferred for provisioning and deprovisioning. SAML group claims are sometimes brittle depending on IdP. If you use Okta, Okta's group push + SCIM is recommended.
[05:58] Jamal Ortiz: Any gotchas on SAML NameID formats and subject confirmation? Our IdP uses transient NameID for some flows.
[06:05] Samir Patel: Transient NameID can work for SSO-only sessions, but for provisioning and persistent mapping we prefer email or persistent NameID. We'll document the recommended configurations — I'll share the metadata.
[06:18] Laura Kim: For our compliance team, can Redwood produce an audit export on demand?
[06:23] Nina Zhou: Yes, we can export audit logs for a tenant as CSV/JSON; for Dedicated/Private we can set up push to your storage so the retention and export are under your control.
[06:34] Priya Narang: Encryption keys — if we use our CMK in AWS, who has ability to decrypt model request metadata?
[06:41] Nina Zhou: Redwood doesn't hold key material for CMK; we perform envelope encryption where your CMK wraps the data key. Access control is governed by your KMS IAM policies; only services with decrypt permission and the runtime components will be able to decrypt when processing. We'll share the architecture diagram.
[07:00] Jamal Ortiz: Request metadata could include prompts; any PII redaction or masking available?
[07:06] Samir Patel: We don't automatically redact PII in inputs; that's typically done by the customer before sending. We do offer middleware for redaction in the Dedicated/Private packages and can recommend patterns. For hosted we provide guidance and some pre-built filters.
[07:22] Laura Kim: What's the separation between control plane and data plane for Private?
[07:27] Nina Zhou: Control plane can be hosted but we offer a private control plane option; data plane always runs in your VPC for Private, so network traffic and keys stay inside. For Dedicated there is a mix — you can opt for a private control plane if required.
[07:42] Priya Narang: About session invalidation — you said 2 minutes window for hosted. Is that SLA'd?
[07:47] Nina Zhou: It's not SLA'd for hosted; it's under best-effort. For Dedicated we can contract a stricter SLA and tune heartbeat/propagation intervals.
[07:58] Jamal Ortiz: Any security reviews or pen tests Redwood has done?
[08:02] Samir Patel: Yes, third-party pen tests and regular fuzzing; details are in the security pack. SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certs are included.
[08:10] Laura Kim: Great. Can you walk through a sample SCIM mapping?
[08:14] Nina Zhou: Sure — sample: scimGroup 'atlas-admins' -> role 'admin', scimGroup 'atlas-devs' -> role 'developer'. We accept externalId for mapping. We'll provide the JSON mapping file.
[08:28] Priya Narang: For contractors we want JIT via SAML and no provisioning in SCIM; how would that be enforced?
[08:35] Nina Zhou: You can set a provisioning rule: only map groups matching 'employee-*' for SCIM provisioning. Contractors can be allowed to SSO with a limited role created specifically for contractors with time-bound access. We can also set expiry on temporary roles.
[08:50] Jamal Ortiz: Is there MFA requirement on admin accounts?
[08:54] Samir Patel: We enforce admin MFA by default for Redwood console logins; if you integrate SSO, MFA is enforced at the IdP side.
[09:03] Laura Kim: Any integrations with SIEMs for alerts?
[09:06] Nina Zhou: Yes, we support syslog, SIEM integrations, and push to Splunk/Datadog via webhook/forwarder.
[09:14] Samir Patel: Quick check — timeline: AtlasMed wants pilot in June, production by Q3 if all good. Is that accurate?
[09:21] Laura Kim: That aligns with our timeline. Security review signoff needs to happen before pilot.
[09:26] Priya Narang: We'll need the SAML metadata and SCIM sample mapping to share with IdP team tomorrow ideally.
[09:33] Samir Patel: We'll send those by EOD. Nina, you'll attach RBAC examples?
[09:38] Nina Zhou: Yep, I'll include role examples and a mapping template.
[09:42] Jamal Ortiz: For the Dedicated pilot, can we get a network diagram and expected egress/IP ranges to allowlist?
[09:48] Samir Patel: Yes, we'll include the network diagram and egress ranges in the security pack. For Private we'd do a design review.
[09:57] Laura Kim: Anything else on key rotation and access reviews?
[09:59] Nina Zhou: We recommend quarterly key rotation for service keys and annual review for CMKs; we support key rotation automation for customer-managed keys.
[10:10] Samir Patel: Ok let's do a quick recap and next steps. Action items: Samir share SAML metadata + security pack; Nina share RBAC mapping + SCIM template; AtlasMed to confirm NameID and group attribute and schedule IdP meeting.
[10:24] Priya Narang: Sounds good. One question — is there a public status or incident feed we can subscribe to?
[10:29] Samir Patel: Yes, we have a status.redwoodai.com feed and support subscriptions for enterprise.
[10:35] Laura Kim: Thanks, that covers it.
[10:37] Samir Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and a proposed IdP meeting invite for next week.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcript contains occasional auto-transcription artifacts (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache in other sessions), speakers sometimes abbreviated. References: security pack link (shared), SAML metadata (to be attached), SCIM mapping template (to be attached).
